findings.issue_text: Member routes are declared without member/collection wrapper causing dynamic segment to be :id, but controller actions require params[:group_id], which will be missing on real requests and raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, breaking add/remove-member in production

Controller specs for add_members/remove_member inject group_id directly into the params hash instead of going through real route/URL parsing, masking the routing/param-name mismatch and letting broken tests pass
totalPages computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, leaving pagination showing a next page past the actual last page
limit param in groups_controller members action is read from client input with no upper bound, allowing unbounded query size
findMembers in group.js now returns undefined for blank names instead of a resolved empty-array promise, breaking the method's promise contract for any caller that chains .then()

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs for add_members/remove_member inject group_id directly into the params hash instead of going through real route/URL parsing, masking the routing/param-name mismatch and letting broken tests pass

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new routes for membership are defined inside `resources :groups` as `put "members"` and `delete "members"`, which in Rails generates member-style routes with the param name `:group_id` (e.g. `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`). The controller actions `add_members`/`remove_member` explicitly `require(:group_id)`, and the specs pass `group_id:` accordingly, so there is no routing/param-name mismatch being “masked” by the tests. (There may be other issues, e.g. HTTP verb mismatch in the truncated spec, but that’s not what this finding claims.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: limit param in groups_controller members action is read from client input with no upper bound, allowing unbounded query size

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is derived directly from `params[:limit]` via `(params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then passed to ActiveRecord `.limit(limit)` with no maximum cap or validation. This lets a client supply an arbitrarily large `limit` (and potentially negative/zero values), causing very large queries and responses. The diff also expands this behavior to all groups (previously pagination/limit logic was only applied for automatic groups).
